extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (prosecution counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to require restriction/election of inventions (including election of species, Markush claims, rejoinder, burden, linking claims, and related signatory/administrative practice) during patent examination under MPEP and relevant statutes/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for restriction (35 U.S.C. 121)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more independent and distinct inventions are claimed in one application, the Director may require the application to be restricted to one of the inventions. If the other invention is made the subject of a divisional application which complies with section 120, it shall be entitled to the benefit of the filing date of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the statutory authority for restriction requirements and for filing divisionals to preserve benefit of original filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory prohibition on claiming independent/distinct inventions together (37 C.F.R. §1.141)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or more independent and distinct inventions may not be claimed in one national application, except more than one species may be claimed if there is an allowable generic claim and species claims in excess of one are dependent or include all limitations of the generic claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows multiple species only when a generic claim is allowable and species claims beyond one are dependent or include the generic limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for restriction procedure (37 C.F.R. §1.142)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or more independent and distinct inventions are claimed in a single application, the examiner in an Office action will require the applicant in the reply to elect an invention to which the claims will be restricted (requirement for restriction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction is effected by an official requirement for election presented in an Office action; applicant must reply with an election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent presentation of claims directed to a different invention (37 C.F.R. §1.145)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after an office action, applicant presents claims directed to an invention distinct from and independent of the invention previously claimed, applicant will be required to restrict the claims to the invention previously claimed if the amendment is entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly presented distinct invention claims presented after an action can trigger a requirement to restrict to the previously claimed invention, subject to reconsideration/review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of species in first action when generic + multiple species present (37 C.F.R. §1.146)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action on an application containing a generic claim and claims to more than one patentably distinct species, the examiner may require the applicant to elect a species to which the claims will be restricted if no claim to the genus is allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may require election of species in first action when genus is not allowable and multiple patentably distinct species are claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting election when more than a reasonable number of species present (§1.146)
rubrics_metrics.description: If such application contains claims directed to more than a reasonable number of species, the examiner may require restriction of claims to not more than a reasonable number of species before taking further action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may limit the number of species examined to a reasonable number to manage burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction proper only if inventions can support separate patents and are independent or distinct (MPEP 803)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may properly be required to be restricted to one of two or more claimed inventions only if they are able to support separate patents and they are either independent or distinct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must evaluate whether separate patents are supportable and determine independence/distinctness per related MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles of distinctness/independence (MPEP 806 summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: (A) Independent inventions (no disclosed relation): restriction ordinarily proper. (B) Related as disclosed but distinct as claimed: restriction may be proper. (C) Related as disclosed but not distinct as claimed: restriction never proper. (D) Reasonable number of species may be claimed when there is an allowable claim generic thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these principles to categorize relationships among claimed inventions before deciding restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare claimed subject matter to determine distinctness/independence (MPEP 806.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: In questions of double patenting and restriction, the claimed subject matter that is asserted must be compared to determine distinctness or independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on claim scope and comparison of claim language rather than solely disclosed embodiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product/process distinction standard (example guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish distinction between a product claim and a process claim, the examiner must show that the product as claimed can be used in a materially different process; a process limited to administering Compound X does not encompass applying ice and is not distinct simply because other processes exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat product/process as distinct unless claim language makes them materially different in claimed scope; analyze what the process claim actually requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single embodiment claims defining same essential features — never restrict (MPEP 806.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims define the same essential characteristics of a single disclosed embodiment, restriction should never be required because the claims are different definitions of the same disclosed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that vary only in breadth/scope over the same embodiment are not distinct inventions for restriction purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Species must be patentably distinct from each other (MPEP 806.04/808.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: In requiring restriction among plural species, the examiner should group species considered clearly unpatentable over each other; election should not be required between species that are considered clearly unpatentable (obvious) over each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If species would have been obvious variants of one another, do not require election; group unpatentable-over-each-other species together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: labels (species) that are obvious over each other — no restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: When various detectable labels for an antibody are known and it would have been obvious to add any of them, the examiner should not require an election among those labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prior art/obviousness analysis to avoid needless restriction among obvious variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express admission of obviousness prevents restriction (In re Lee)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an express admission that the claimed inventions would have been obvious over each other, restriction should not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions in the record that claims are obviously related remove the basis for restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush group members few/closely related — examine all members (MPEP 803.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If members of a Markush group are few or so closely related that a search/examination of entire claim can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine all members even if directed to independent/distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No provisional election or provisional species election when full examination is practicable without serious burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional election of species for Markush-type claims (MPEP 803.02/808.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Markush-type claims encompassing at least two independent/distinct inventions, the examiner may require a provisional election of a single species prior to examination on the merits, using form paragraph 8.01 or 8.02 as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional election narrows initial examination to elected species; non-elected species may be held withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination practice after election for Markush claims (MPEP 803.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following election, the Markush-type claim is examined fully with respect to the elected species and further to the extent necessary to determine patentability. If the elected species is rejected as anticipated or obvious, the Markush claim and elected species are rejected and nonelected species are held withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner need not extend search to all nonelected species; provisional election limits examination unless overcome by applicant amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: If prior art is found on a nonelected species (MPEP 803.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If prior art is found that anticipates or renders obvious the Markush-type claim with respect to a nonelected species, the Markush claim shall be rejected and nonelected species held withdrawn; the prior art search will not be extended unnecessarily to cover all nonelected species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner's search is not required to cover all nonelected species broadly once rejection is found for a nonelected species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant can amend Markush claim to remove problematic species and have reexamination extended (MPEP 803.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant overcomes a rejection by amending the Markush-type claim to exclude the species anticipated or rendered obvious, the amended Markush claim will be reexamined and examination extended as necessary to determine patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant amendments can restore broader examination of the Markush claim when prior-art issues are removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to election-by-original-presentation practice (MPEP 821.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Election-by-original-presentation does not apply where a provisional election of a species was made and applicant later cancels the elected species, or where applicant presents claims that could not have been restricted from earlier claims had they been presented earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newly added claims that would not have been restrictable earlier should be entered and examined along with existing claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: New dependent or newly added species claims that would not have been restrictable earlier should be entered (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment adds dependent claims or newly added species claims that would not have been restrictable from the existing claims had they been presented earlier, the new claims should be entered and examined with the existing claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not improperly exclude newly presented claims from examination when earlier presentation would not have allowed restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election required after action on the merits when species claims presented (MPEP 808.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant presents species claims to more than one patentably distinct species after an Office action on only generic claims, the Office may require the applicant to elect a single species for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing matters: species presented after an action on the merits can trigger an election requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction only when generic claims encompass multiplicity causing unduly extensive/burdensome search (MPEP 808.01/803.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: In applications with only generic claims, restriction cannot be required unless the generic claims recite or encompass such multiplicity of species that an unduly extensive and burdensome search would be necessary to search the entire scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether burden of full search justifies restriction; do not restrict merely because multiple species are possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of burden — examiner must examine when no serious burden (MPEP 803.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search and examination of all claims can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits even though they include claims to independent or distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden is the key practical criterion; same classification/field of search with no separate future classification indicates no reason to divide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot restrict among already-examined claims after full action on the merits (MPEP 803.02/808.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following a first action on the merits of all claims, a later examiner cannot properly require restriction amongst already-examined claims; the Office cannot establish burden after prior full examination to support a new requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full faith and credit should be given to prior examiner's search and action unless clear error or new prior art exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final restriction actions (MPEP 803.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an examiner with permanent full signatory authority or temporary full signatory authority may sign final Office actions containing a final requirement for restriction. Examiners with partial signatory authority may sign non-final Office actions containing a final requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative requirement to ensure supervisory review/authority for final restriction requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking claims must be examined with the linked invention; effect on restriction (MPEP 809)
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking claims are examined with and considered part of the elected invention. When all claims directed to the elected invention are allowable, and any linking claim is allowable, the restriction between the linked inventions must be withdrawn and any nonelected claim depending from the allowable linking claim must be rejoined and fully examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowable linking/generic claims require reconsideration of restriction and possible rejoinder of previously withdrawn claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant entitled to retain nonelected claims when restriction predicated on nonallowability of linking claims (MPEP 809)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where restriction is predicated upon nonallowability of generic or linking claims, applicant is entitled to retain in the application claims to the nonelected invention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention protects applicant's rights pending resolution of linking/generic claim allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance of linking or generic claims — notification and reinstatement (MPEP 809)
rubrics_metrics.description: When withdrawn claims were canceled pursuant to restriction but a linking claim is later allowed, the examiner must notify applicant that any canceled nonelected claims depending from the allowable linking claim may be reinstated by amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must provide opportunity for applicant to reinstate canceled nonelected claims upon allowance of linking claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demarcation — indicate exactly how application is to be restricted (MPEP 814)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must provide a clear and detailed record of the restriction requirement to show the demarcation between restricted inventions so it can be determined whether continuing-application claims are consonant with the restriction and subject to the 35 U.S.C. 121 protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete, precise restriction statements are needed for downstream double-patenting/determinations and for applicant/continuation filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the restriction requirement complete (MPEP 815)
rubrics_metrics.description: When making a restriction requirement, every effort should be made to have the requirement complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid incomplete or ambiguous restriction statements that complicate prosecution and continuation practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must make their own election (MPEP 818.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must make the election; the examiner will not make the election for the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant's strategic choice; examiner's role is to present the requirement, not to select on applicant's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsider restriction at time of allowance; rejoinder practice (MPEP 821.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: The propriety of a restriction requirement should be reconsidered when all claims directed to the elected invention are in condition for allowance, and nonelected inventions should be considered for rejoinder (withdrawal of restriction and examination of formerly nonelected inventions on the merits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoinder is triggered by allowance of elected claims; examiner should evaluate and rejoin appropriate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoined claims must be fully examined for patentability (MPEP 821.04 / 37 C.F.R. 1.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejoined claims must be fully examined for patentability and must meet all criteria including 35 U.S.C. 101, 102, 103 and 112 to be allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoinder does not relax substantive patentability requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: When restriction must be withdrawn and double patenting caution (MPEP 821.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: When inventions are rejoined the restriction must be withdrawn. Any claims in a continuation or divisional that are anticipated by or obvious over claims of the parent may be subject to a double patenting rejection when restriction is withdrawn in the parent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of double patenting implications when withdrawing restriction — claims in continuations/divisionals might be vulnerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving applicant rights under 35 U.S.C. 121 (third sentence) (MPEP 821.04(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant cancels all claims directed to a nonelected process invention before rejoinder occurs, the examiner should not withdraw the restriction requirement. This preserves applicant's rights under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation of nonelected claims prior to rejoinder can preserve statutory protections tied to original restriction/divisional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder practice applies to national stage applications (MPEP 1893.05(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For national stage applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 371, if the examiner determines lack of unity and requires election, when all claims drawn to the elected invention are allowable, the nonelected invention(s) should be considered for rejoinder; any nonelected product claim that requires all limitations of an allowable product claim, and nonelected process claims that require all limitations of an allowable process claim, should be rejoined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejoinder rules extend to national stage/PCT national entry practice; apply unity principles in light of PCT unity for PCT-originated filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynucleotide/nucleotide sequence applications — apply 800 chapter standards (OG Notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: For U.S. national applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), polynucleotide molecules will be subject to the standards for requiring restriction or provisional election of species set forth in MPEP Chapter 800, and will be considered for independence, relatedness, distinction and burden as for any other molecule. For PCTs and national stage filings, unity of invention determination will be made in view of PCT rules; unity exists when molecules, as claimed, share a general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the same restriction/election/burden standards to nucleotide sequence claims; for PCT-originated filings, use PCT unity principles when assessing national stage claims.
